summary: Improvement remains strategically coherent, but the canonical priority surface was stale and has now been refreshed. The most important learning since yesterday is that Improvement scope materially expanded from interface rollout/maintenance into explicit ownership of the minimum cross-system measurement-and-follow-up standard for recurring loops, starting with the overnight loop. That is a real planning delta: the former Priority 3 rollout gap has largely moved into maintenance, while the new live gap is applying the overnight minimum-performance standard and ledger contract in a lightweight, auditable way. Priority 1 remains the strongest structural bottleneck, Priority 2 remains the clearest unchanged execution gap, and the refreshed Priority 3 now reflects the new control-layer responsibility rather than yesterday’s already-mostly-complete rollout posture.
materialChanges: TOP_PRIORITIES.md was stale relative to the full product stack and was updated in this run: the former Priority 3 interface-rollout item moved to watch/maintenance, and a new Priority 3 now captures the newly codified minimum cross-system measurement-and-follow-up responsibility starting with the overnight loop.
Internal product state changed on 2026-03-23: OPERATING_MODEL.md, PLAN.md, and DECISIONS.md were updated to make lightweight performance/follow-up ownership explicit, including D-005.
Two new control artifacts now exist and materially change execution expectations: OVERNIGHT_LOOP_MINIMUM_PERFORMANCE_STANDARD_V1.md and OVERNIGHT_LOOP_LEDGER_CONTRACT_V1.md.
No new execution evidence appeared for Priority 2; pinned-lane delivery into PXS still shows no visible operational progress.

The previously dominant interface-rollout gap is no longer the main open planning problem because active-product first-deployment coverage and the reusable standard reference set were already completed before this run.
mostImportantLearningSinceYesterday: Improvement is no longer only defining how signals become improvement work; it now also owns the minimum proof that recurring operational loops are running, helping, and auditable. That shifts the immediate planning gap from more rollout-definition work toward lightweight live control application for the overnight loop.

externalChangesSinceYesterday.implication: This strengthens Improvement’s new overnight auditability/verification posture and Priority 2’s version-truth/verification rationale, but it does not justify a priority reorder on its own.

externalChangesSinceYesterday.implication: Improvement remains internally driven this cycle; external signals are contextual reinforcement, not primary steering input.

keyImplications: Priority refresh was required and completed in code.
The product’s next non-execution planning focus is now lightweight operational control proof, not additional rollout-definition work.
The major unchanged gap remains pinned-lane deployment into PXS.

topPriorities.title: Converge improvement execution into one canonical TDE-first system of record
topPriorities.why: Improvement still needs one explicit, reusable, evidence-backed execution path; otherwise signals can fragment across non-canonical surfaces and weaken traceability.
topPriorities.currentStatus: The low-risk Phase 1 substrate is selected in D-003 and is now supported by PLAN, OPERATING_MODEL, INTERFACES, TDE entry-surface alignment, and exemplar validation around OPS-2026-066 through OPS-2026-069. The remaining gap is disciplined ongoing live reuse and explicit disposition through the canonical execution system rather than substrate ambiguity.
topPriorities.nextStep: Use the aligned Phase 1 substrate as the default live operating path and drive the validated exemplar batch toward explicit disposition so the substrate is visibly exercised in canonical execution, not just codified.

topPriorities.title: Ship A-005 into PXS through a pinned lane with version truth, rollback, and verification semantics
topPriorities.why: Improvement delivery still depends on interim-copy behavior, so downstream drift risk remains active and installed-state truth is weak.
topPriorities.currentStatus: No new progress is visible in the reviewed product stack or execution evidence. Interim-copy lanes still appear to be the baseline mechanism, and the pinned-lane target is not yet the lived distribution path.
topPriorities.nextStep: Implement the pinned lane as an operational path with machine-checkable installed-version truth, explicit rollback behavior, and a verification pass that closes the interim-drift gap.

topPriorities.title: Operationalize the minimum cross-system measurement-and-follow-up standard, starting with the overnight loop
topPriorities.why: Improvement now explicitly owns the minimum standard for proving whether recurring loops ran, helped, and remain auditable. Without lightweight live application, the overnight system can repeat activity without clearly surfacing stuckness or contribution.
topPriorities.currentStatus: D-005, OPERATING_MODEL.md, and PLAN.md now codify this responsibility. The standard and ledger contract exist, but live application has not yet become visible as a recurring canonical control record.
topPriorities.nextStep: Apply the overnight minimum-performance standard in a lightweight way by maintaining the compact canonical ledger entry for each night so run health, contribution, and stuckness can be assessed without a heavy reporting layer.

constraints: Improvement must remain evidence-backed and must not become a narrative-only reporting layer.
Improvement does not own canonical task or decision state; that boundary remains with Task Management / TDE.
The new measurement/follow-up responsibility is intentionally narrow and should not expand into broad reporting bureaucracy.
No authority or security boundary changes should be made as part of improvement rollout without explicit escalation.

risksOrOpportunities.title: Improvement signals do not convert reliably into owned execution
risksOrOpportunities.note: The proof case is closed, the reference batch exists, and active-product rollout is complete. The remaining risk is sustained reuse and disposition discipline rather than definition.

risksOrOpportunities.title: Status truth drifts inside the improvement product itself
risksOrOpportunities.note: A stale priority surface was detected and corrected in this run rather than left implicit.

risksOrOpportunities.title: New measurement scope could expand into process overhead
risksOrOpportunities.note: The overnight standard is intentionally narrow; the main control risk is turning a lean auditability layer into a reporting burden.

risksOrOpportunities.title: Use the overnight ledger as the first bounded proof that Improvement can own lightweight follow-up without creating bureaucracy
risksOrOpportunities.note: A successful narrow implementation would give the portfolio a reusable control pattern for other recurring loops.

researchDelta: External scanning found contextual reinforcement rather than steering change. Fresh CI/CD compromise reporting increases the value of auditable verification and lightweight control records, but no external development displaced the internal product stack as the main driver of tonight’s refresh. The material delta was internal: D-005 plus the new overnight standard and ledger contract changed what Improvement should treat as an active top priority.

proposedNextActions.rationale: The rollout gap has shifted from deployment to maintenance; it still matters, but it is no longer the top planning delta.
